text:
alex: hitting 401s from Redwood hosted API only when I deploy a bundled Next app. Local node run against same code is fine (200). thought it was auth but token is set the same way for both environments. repro: 1) yarn build -> next start (server) -> ok 2) yarn build -> vercel edge -> 401. bundle uses webpack 5 via next 13.
anya: sorry for the outage, assigning. can you paste package.json + exports + how you import the sdk? also which sdk version?
alex: sdk @redwood/inference v1.6.2. package.json snippet: ````json
{"name":"app","version":"0.1.0","type":"module","exports":{"./package.json":"./package.json","./":"./dist/index.mjs","./node":"./dist/index.cjs"},"dependencies":{"@redwood/inference":"^1.6.2"}}
````
import code: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` and `const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })`
anya: thanks. two quick asks: 1) can you share a small network log showing the failing request headers? 2) can you try `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference/node'` to force node entry?
alex: network dump from edge function (incognito capture): ````
POST /v1/generate 401
Request headers:
  host: api.redwood.ai
  user-agent: Next.js Edge
  authorization: undefined
  content-type: application/json
Response: {"error":"Unauthorized"} request-id: r-3f2a
````
alex: switching to `@redwood/inference/node` in code + redeploy -> SUCCESS on SSR serverless (200) but still 401 on Edge runtime.
sam: likely root cause: bundler is picking the browser/edge entry that doesn't accept env-inlined keys or there's a conditional exports mismatch. in some bundlers `process.env.*` gets inlined at build time; in edge builds env might not be available and becomes undefined. also `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` may resolve to a browser ESM shim that expects a different auth flow. try: 1) ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is available to the runtime (server/edge) via platform env, not client-side expose. 2) pin import to node entry when doing SSR: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference/node'` or require CJS when running node.
julian: additional edge note — Vercel Edge runtime doesn't have node globals; many SDKs ship a light browser build that intentionally strips long-lived secrets. If you accidentally bundle the browser build into an edge function and also inline `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` at build time, the token can become `undefined` or stripped for security. For Edge you need to pass the key at runtime to the server-side handler, not embed it in client bundle.
alex: that matches: we were using a next middleware to set the header from process.env at build time for some reason. changed to read env at runtime in the server handler and it works on edge too. thanks.
anya: good find. i still want to add two things for our SDK: 1) better error message when Authorization header missing (right now server returns generic 401), 2) doc blurb about conditional exports and bundlers causing unexpected browser entry selection. i'll escalate.
ops_oncall: noted. i'll create a small runtime sentinel in the next SDK patch — before sending a request, if `Authorization` header is falsy, throw an informative client-side error pointing at common bundler/env causes instead of letting it go to upstream 401. will also add a log with request-id when we receive 401 to make repros easier.
dev_support_bot: created ticket INF-7843 linking logs r-3f2a and the package.json snippet. escalation to eng-runtime assigned to @sam.
alex: thanks everyone — redeploying with runtime env read, will follow up if anything else shows up. :thumbsup:
